stem: In tool (function) calling, who executes the tool?

options.text: The model executes it inside its weights
The application code, after the model returns a structured request naming the tool and its arguments
The embedding service
The end user

explanation: The model only proposes a call as structured output. The surrounding application validates the request, runs the tool, and returns the result to the model. That boundary is where authorisation and validation belong.

stem: When is a fixed workflow (prompt chain or router) usually preferable to an autonomous agent loop?

options.text: When the steps are known in advance and predictability, cost and testability matter
When nothing about the task is known
When you want the model to choose its own tools indefinitely
When latency does not matter at all

explanation: Known, stable steps are cheaper, faster, easier to test and easier to audit as a workflow. Agents earn their cost when the path cannot be specified in advance.

stem: Which is a genuine drawback of splitting a task across many cooperating agents?

options.text: Multi-agent systems cannot use tools
Coordination overhead, compounding errors between agents, higher cost and harder debugging
They always run slower than one agent in every case
They cannot be evaluated

explanation: Every handoff adds tokens, latency and a new place to lose or distort information. Multi-agent designs are justified by clear specialisation or parallelism, not by default.

stem: A bank wants an assistant for card-dispute intake. The process has six fixed steps with mandatory checks. A prototype using a free-roaming agent skips steps about one time in twenty.
constraints: Some free-text understanding is needed to read customer descriptions

options.text: Implement the six steps as an explicit workflow with deterministic ordering, using the model for language understanding inside individual steps and logging each step.
Keep the free-roaming agent and add a stronger instruction to never skip steps.
Add more agents that supervise the first agent.
Abandon the model and use only a web form.

rationales.text: Mandatory ordering is better enforced by code than by a prompt instruction.
Instructions to a model are a guarantee of behaviour.
Models still add value in understanding free text within a step.
More supervising agents remove the need for deterministic control.

explanation: When the path is known and compliance requires it, encode it in the control flow and use the model for sub-tasks. Prompt instructions reduce but do not eliminate deviation.
model_answer: Make the sequence deterministic, keep model calls scoped and schema-validated, log each step for audit, and test the workflow with adversarial and ambiguous inputs.

stem: An analytics assistant must answer questions needing SQL generation, document reading and chart drafting. A single agent with fifteen tools often picks the wrong tool and loses track in long sessions.
constraints: Latency target under 15 seconds for common questions

options.text: Introduce a supervisor that routes to a few specialised sub-agents or sub-flows with narrow tool sets, keep shared state explicit, and compare against the single-agent baseline on the evaluation set including latency.
Add five more tools to the single agent for coverage.
Run every sub-agent for every question in parallel and merge answers.
Lower the temperature to zero and accept the errors.

rationales.text: Narrower tool sets reduce selection errors.
More tools always improves coverage without cost.
A baseline comparison shows whether the added complexity pays for itself.

explanation: Specialisation with routing can reduce tool confusion, but the extra coordination must justify itself against a baseline. Running everything in parallel wastes cost and may reduce quality.
model_answer: Route to specialised components with small tool sets, define the shared state and handoff format, measure accuracy and latency versus the single-agent baseline, and keep the simplest design that meets targets.

rubric.criterion: Proposes routing and narrow tool sets
